description: A project's ratio is the mean of its per-record boxx/boxz ratios.

c.request: Match each spatial record (`scanspatial`) to the project whose `arcregistry` equals its `arcref`, and drop records with no matching project. What is each project's bounding-box X-to-Z ratio (`boxx` to `boxz`), ignoring missing values? Which 10 projects beat the simple average ratio of the projects in their own funding source (`projects.fundflux`) by the widest margin? Show the project ID, funding source, ratio and margin, sorted by margin from largest to smallest (missing last), with no rounding. A project's ratio is the mean of its per-record boxx/boxz ratios.
c.sql: WITH project_ratios AS (SELECT p.arcregistry, p.fundflux, AVG(s.boxx / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS ratio FROM scanspatial AS s JOIN projects AS p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.arcregistry, p.fundflux), compared AS (SELECT arcregistry, fundflux, ratio, ratio - AVG(ratio) OVER (PARTITION BY fundflux) AS margin FROM project_ratios) SELECT arcregistry AS project_id, fundflux AS funding_source, ratio, margin FROM compared WHERE margin > 0 ORDER BY margin DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

a.request: Match each spatial record (`scanspatial`) to the project whose `arcregistry` equals its `arcref`, and drop records with no matching project. For each project ID and its funding source (`projects.fundflux`), work out the project's X-to-Z ratio like this: first compute `boxx` ÷ `boxz` separately for each of its spatial records, then average those per-record ratios, ignoring missing ones. Within each funding source, take the simple average of its projects' ratios. Then return the 10 projects whose ratio is above their funding source's average by the most. Sort them by that excess from largest to smallest, with missing values last. Show the project ID, funding source, ratio and excess, with no rounding.
a.sql: WITH project_ratios AS (SELECT p.arcregistry AS project_id, p.fundflux AS funding_source, AVG(s.boxx / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS ratio FROM scanspatial AS s JOIN projects AS p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.arcregistry, p.fundflux), compared AS (SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, ratio - AVG(ratio) OVER (PARTITION BY funding_source) AS excess FROM project_ratios) SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, excess FROM compared WHERE excess > 0 ORDER BY excess DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

b.request: For each project with matching `scanspatial` records, calculate the mean of its nonmissing per-record `boxx / boxz` ratios; compare that project ratio with the simple average of project ratios for projects with the same `fundflux`; return the 10 projects with the largest positive margins, showing project ID, funding source, ratio, and unrounded margin, sorted by margin descending with missing margins last
b.sql: WITH project_ratios AS (SELECT p.arcregistry, p.fundflux, AVG(s.boxx / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS ratio FROM projects AS p JOIN scanspatial AS s ON s.arcref = p.arcregistry GROUP BY p.arcregistry, p.fundflux), compared AS (SELECT arcregistry, fundflux, ratio, ratio - AVG(ratio) OVER (PARTITION BY fundflux) AS margin FROM project_ratios) SELECT arcregistry AS project_id, fundflux AS funding_source, ratio, margin FROM compared WHERE margin > 0 OR margin IS NULL ORDER BY margin IS NULL, margin DESC LIMIT 10;

d.request: Match each `scanspatial` record to the project whose `arcregistry` equals the record’s `arcref`, and drop unmatched records. For each project, calculate its bounding-box X-to-Z ratio as the mean of its nonmissing per-record `boxx/boxz` ratios. Which 10 projects exceed the simple average project ratio for their funding source (`projects.fundflux`) by the widest margin? Show the project ID, funding source, ratio, and margin, sorted by margin from largest to smallest with missing values last, and do not round.
d.sql: WITH project_ratios AS (SELECT p.arcregistry AS project_id, p.fundflux AS funding_source, AVG(s.boxx / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS ratio FROM scanspatial AS s JOIN projects AS p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.arcregistry, p.fundflux), compared AS (SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, ratio - AVG(ratio) OVER (PARTITION BY funding_source) AS margin FROM project_ratios) SELECT project_id, funding_source, ratio, margin FROM compared WHERE margin > 0 ORDER BY margin DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
